Rakesh Kumar Cnr No.: Dlse01-005176-2019 1. Sh. Ranjeet Chaudhary S/o Sh. Satyender Chaudhary R/o G-96, Gali no.10 Anand Parwat, New Delhi. ........Petitioner Versus 1. Sh. Rakesh Kumar Mahawar S/o Sh. Bhore Lal R/o D-429, Sakur Basti, New Delhi ............Driver/Respondent no.1 2. texts.facts: The present claim arises out of a detailed accident report (DAR), filed by the police in terms of the provision of Motor Vehicle Act in which petitioner Ranjit Chaudhary (aged about 40 years) , one Subham and one Ashish sustained injuries. Ranjeet Chaudhary (Dar) vs Rakesh Kumar(124/19Lc) on 22 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3205587/ 1 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 17.05.2019, one Ashish Soni alongwith one Subham were travelling in an Auto bearing no.DL-1RQ-6064 for Mayapuri. At about 4.45 PM, when they reached at traffic signal of India Habitate Center, a green bus bearing no.DL-1PC-7774 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) came at a high speed and hit the auto. Both the persons alongwith driver of such auto were admitted to AIIMS hospital. Statement of injured namely Subham and Ashish were recorded. Statement of Ranjit Chaudhary could not be recorded as he was under the Red Zone. 3. An FIR no. 0124/2020 dated 18.05.2019 u/s 279/337 IPC was registered against the driver of the offending vehicle. After investigation, chargesheet was filed before concerned criminal court against the driver of the offending vehicle while present DAR was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is driver, Respondent no.2 is owner and Respondent no.3 is the insurance company of the offending vehicle. 5. Respondent no.1 and 2 filed their reply submitting that MACT NO.556/19 Ranjeet Chaudhary v. Rakesh Kumar P.No. 2 Of 21 BK driver of offending vehicle was not at fault as he started the bus when traffic signal turned green while Auto driver tried to cross the road on yellow signal from other side. In the middle of the road, auto driver tried to apply brake but could not manage and dashed into the bus near its Emergency Door resulting in the accident. It is pleaded that auto driver was himself negligent. However, offending vehicle was insured on the date of accident. Respondent no.3/insurance company filed its reply denying the negligence of Respondent no.1 and claiming accident to have occurred due to sole negligence of the petitioner. It is however not denied that the offending vehicle was insured with Respondent no.3 at the time of accident. 6. Vide order dated 17.12.2019, following issues were framed. 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 17.05.2019 due to rash and negligent driving of driver of vehicle no. DL-1Pc-7774 being driven by R1, owned by R-2 and insured with R-3? OPP 2. Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom? OPP. 3. Relief. 7. Evidence was recorded through learned Local Commissioner. To prove his claim, petitioner Ranjit Chaudhary led his evidence by examining himself as PW-1 by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He reiterated the facts as of the DAR. On 17.05.2019 after the accident, he was shifted to Jai Prakash Narayan Apex Trauma Center, AIIMS hospital for treatment. He suffered fracture distal radius left and fracture tibial proximal MACT NO.556/19 Ranjeet Chaudhary v. Rakesh Kumar P.No. 3 Of 21 BK right side and sustained abrasions, wounds and other grievous injuries all over his body. After some treatment, he was transferred to other hospital on 18.05.2019. On 21.05.2019, he was admitted in Dr. Ram Manohar Lohiya Hospital for treatment,operated on 23.05.2019 and discharged on 23.05.2019. Further, on the same day i.e. 25.05.2019, he was again admitted and Ranjeet Chaudhary (Dar) vs Rakesh Kumar(124/19Lc) on 22 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3205587/ 2 operated, a set of implants were inserted in his left leg and discharged on 27.05.2019. Thereafter, he took regular treatment in Ortho OPD. Several tests, X-rays and dressing was done on all alternate days from time to time. He incurred Rs.1,50,000/- on special diet, conveyance, treatment and medicines. He further deposed that was working as TSR driver and earning Rs.18,000/- p.m. As he suffered fracture on his right leg and left forearm and implants are also inserted, therefore, he would be able to drive TSR in future. He engaged an attendant for four months, whom he paid Rs.36,000/- @Rs.300/- per day. He relied upon documents i.e. Aadhar card as Ex.PW-1/1, transfer form and MLC as Ex.PW-1/2, discharge summary dated 25.05.2019 as Ex.PW-1/3, discharge summary dated 27.05.2019 as Ex.PW-1/4, Ortho OPD card as Ex.PW-1/5, medical bills as Ex.PW-1/6, driving licence as Ex.PW-1/7, photograph of petitioner as Ex.PW-1/8. He was cross-examined by Ld. counsel for insurance company and the cross was adopted by Respondent no.1& 2. No evidence has been led on behalf of the respondents. 8. Final arguments in details were addressed on behalf of the claimant/injured and the insurance company.
texts.arguments: Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & Ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. He has deposed that the accident occurred at the time when he was driving through Lodhi Road from Maxmuller Marg towards Madarasa. He has categorically deposed that the traffic signal was green for him at the time and it is the offending bus that jumped the red signal from its side and dashed into the auto of the victim. Testimony of the petitioner/PW-1 is further corroborated by the DAR and the investigation carried out by the investigating officer. The same is also supported by the MACT NO.556/19 Ranjeet Chaudhary v. Rakesh Kumar P.No. 5 Of 21 BK statements of one Ashish who was one of the passengers in the auto driven by the Ranjeet Chaudhary (Dar) vs Rakesh Kumar(124/19Lc) on 22 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3205587/ 3 victim/petitioner. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. In totality of circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner has been able to prove on the scales of MACT NO.556/19 Ranjeet Chaudhary v. Rakesh Kumar P.No. 6 Of 21 BK preponderance of probabilities that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver/respondent no.1 as well as contributed by the petitioner. 15. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). 16.2. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities MACT NO.556/19 Ranjeet Chaudhary v. Rakesh Kumar P.No. 8 Of 21 BK (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 16.6. Observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajkumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. is quoted hereunder: "10. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps. On such deposits being made, the insurance company shall submit a letter to the MACT NO.556/19 Ranjeet Chaudhary v. Rakesh Kumar P.No. 15 Of 21 BK Nazir of this Tribunal enclosing a copy of the said bank advice, in prescribed format as above, as per which the deposit made to the bank account of this Tribunal, to enable this Tribunal to keep tab on the deposits made and the MCOPs for which they were made. 28. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: Ranjeet Chaudhary (Dar) vs Rakesh Kumar(124/19Lc) on 22 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3205587/ 10 " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". But if the Tribunal is satisfied for reasons to be stated in writing that the whole or part of the amount is required for expanding an existing business or for purchasing some property for earning a livelihood, MACT NO.556/19 Ranjeet Chaudhary v. Rakesh Kumar P.No. 17 Of 21 BK The MACT NO.556/19 Ranjeet Chaudhary v. Rakesh Kumar P.No. 18 Of 21 BK guidelines were not to be understood to mean that the Tribunals were to take a rigid stand while considering an application seeking release of the money.
